paper.title_en: Task-resolved algebraic compatibility and gradient geometry in variational quantum models
paper.abstract_en: Understanding trainability in variational quantum models requires separating the task-relevant signal available to a model from the geometry through which a concrete parametrization converts that signal into gradients. We develop a task-resolved Lie-algebraic framework that separates these effects. The dynamical Lie algebra is distinguished from the instantaneous tangent space realized at a given parameter configuration, and the accessible first-order signal is decomposed into its total amount and its density across independent directions. We derive an exact geometric characterization of these quantities, establish restriction and invariance properties, and show that compatibility acquires a direct gradient-variance interpretation only under isotropic directional sampling. For actual circuits, an additional tangent-frame geometry is required to relate accessible signal to parameter gradients. Numerical experiments validate this decomposition: task-relevant directions may be present in the dynamical algebra but absent from the instantaneous tangent space, ansätze with identical algebraic dimension can exhibit markedly different task alignment, and real tangent frames are strongly anisotropic. In scaling experiments, pooled gradient decay is explained by causal-cone dilution rather than systematic suppression of comparable active directions, while idle extensions leave active compatibility and gradient statistics unchanged. The framework therefore isolates a structural component of first-order trainability without identifying compatibility itself with a barren-plateau criterion.
